image_description: A disassembled bassoon resting horizontally in a dark, velvet-lined instrument case. The image shows the main wooden body sections (boot joint, wing joint, long joint) and the metal bell section, all featuring a deep reddish-brown polished wood finish and complex silver keywork. A curved metal bocal is visible inserted into one of the joints.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although disassembled, the multiple long wooden sections clearly indicate an instrument of significant length when assembled.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument is disassembled and lying horizontally in a case; the assembled U-shape silhouette is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Internal bore structure cannot be visually verified from the exterior of the disassembled instrument.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A curved metal tube (bocal) is clearly visible inserted into the upper joint section.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Complex silver keywork and mechanisms are densely distributed across all visible wooden sections.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell is present but detached/lying down; the 'held diagonally' context is absent as it is in a case.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood exhibits the characteristic deep reddish-brown polished finish typical of maple bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keywork is clearly silver-colored metal.
Visible sections are clearly constructed from turned wooden tubes.

artifact_observations.location: Wood grain on the lower joint
artifact_observations.reasoning: The wood grain appears slightly smudged and lacks the fine, crisp linear detail expected in high-resolution macro photography of polished wood, suggesting mild AI smoothing.

artifact_observations.location: Keywork mechanism near the center strap holder
artifact_observations.reasoning: Some of the thin metal rods and keys appear to merge slightly into the wood or each other without clear mechanical separation or pivot points, a common AI artifact in complex machinery.
The parallel lines of the case interior show very slight warping, though this could also be lens distortion; marked as minor potential artifact.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of woodwind instrument and distinguish it from similar instruments like the contrabassoon or oboe.
To verify that the complex metal keys are distinct entities from the wood and do not suffer from fusion artifacts.
To assess the realism of the wood texture and lighting reflections on the metal parts.
To ensure the instrument sits correctly within the case depth and does not float or clip through the velvet lining.

focus_areas: Integrity of metal keywork connections to wood body
Correct identification of bassoon components (bocal, bell, joints)
Physical plausibility of instrument placement in case
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the mechanical logic of the keywork. AI often generates 'gibberish' keys that don't connect to rods properly. Verify if the bocal insertion point looks physically valid. Check if the wood grain looks procedural/repetitive rather than natural.
